newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel alleges PLO plot, PLO calls it "big lie".
newsitem.headline: Israel alleges PLO plot, PLO calls it "big lie".

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday accused Palestinians of plotting violence but PLO officials called it "a big lie" to divert attention from his plans to settle more Jews on occupied Arab land.

Netanyahu said PLO leader Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority had been planning unrest even before he reinstated financial incentives for Jews to settle in the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip where Palestinians hope to have a state.

"There is clear information that the Palestinian side, senior elements on the Palestinian side, have been planning, without connection to the government decision, for weeks, planning another wave of violence," he told Israel Radio.

Netanyahu said he told U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk of his government's decision before it was formally taken. Washington called the aid to settlers, given after guerrillas killed a settler and her son last week, "troubling".
Anticipating Netanyahu's attack, President Arafat was quoted by an Israeli daily saying Jewish settlement was a time bomb -- and Netanyahu had turned to "cheap propoganda" because he knew it.

Arafat told reporters in Gaza on Sunday: "As for the statements of the Israeli prime minister today that we are preparing to wage war on them, this is untrue and aims at diverting attention from what he is preparing to do against us ...This government does not want peace."

Netanyahu also criticised Israeli opposition parties, who have warned the policies he has pursued since taking office in June, will destroy the Arab-Israeli peace process launched by the previous Labour government in 1991.
Netanyahu said the Israeli opposition should instead be attacking "the clear attempt by the Palestinian Authority to ignite the area."

Major General Abdel-Razek al-Majaydeh, head of Palestinian security forces in the PLO-ruled Gaza Strip enclave, said the PLO feared the Israeli leader could be building a pretext for aggression against Palestinian self-rule enclaves.
"It's a big lie...I'm afraid that by this lie they might carry out aggressive action against the Palestinian territories and they are using this lie as a pretext," Majaydeh said.
Arafat was quoted by Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily as saying: "Instead of implementing what the agreements demand, they decide to expand settlements.
"Netanyahu knows that's a time bomb with many risks...Talk of us igniting the territories is cheap propoganda which belies unclean intentions."
Netanyahu dismissed as inaccurate reports that security chiefs have warned him settlement expansion would cause violence.

His opening of an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem in September spurred clashes in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed. Local media said security chiefs had warned it would spark clashes.
He hinted there would come a time for new Jewish settlements on occupied land. Since taking office, he has approved plans to build thousands of homes in existing settlements.
"It is correct that we will decide at our own timing, in our own way, on expanding on new territories," Netanyahu said.

Opposition leader Shimon Peres told Israel Radio Netanyahu was killing the peace process begun by his government, which lost May elections: "There is not a lot of time for the people of Israel...a window of opportunity that is rapidly closing."
